Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) shows a curvilinear opacity on the right side running parallel to the right heart border, characteristic of the scimitar vein, along with mediastinal deviation to the right and a hypoplastic right lung. The CT images confirm the presence of an abnormal systemic artery supplying the right lower lobe (indicated by arrows in Figures 1 and 5), which is located inferiorly relative to the main pulmonary vasculature. This constellation of findings defines Scimitar syndrome.
